dedupe_keys.name: greencloud energy aware data centre simulator

description: GreenCloud is a packet-level simulator for energy-aware cloud computing data centres with a focus on cloud communications. It models in fine detail the energy consumed by data-centre IT equipment, meaning servers, network switches and links, with independent energy models for CPU, memory, storage and networking resources, and supports virtualisation and virtual-machine migration, so that researchers can study monitoring, resource allocation, workload scheduling and communication protocols. It was developed at the University of Luxembourg within the GreenIT and ECO-CLOUD projects as an extension of the well-known ns-2 network simulator, and user and developer manuals are provided. Coverage: user-defined data-centre architectures such as two-tier, three-tier and high-speed three-tier topologies, without real site data. Format and access: C++ and OTcl source on top of ns-2, downloaded with documentation from the project website; free of charge under the GNU General Public License. Caveats: built on ns-2, which is no longer maintained, so installation on current systems is hard; cooling and power distribution are not modelled. Simulation uses: optimisation and capacity planning of data-centre energy use and networks, resilience of scheduling to failures, and energy-related environmental studies of digital infrastructure. Related records: CloudSim, CloudSim Plus and SimGrid are alternative data-centre simulators; ns-3 is the successor of ns-2.
